critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL (fixed) — /app/frontend/src/pages/JobDetail.js used `myApp` on lines 101/106/108/110 without declaring the state. Any logged-in non-admin candidate viewing /jobs/:id would trigger `ReferenceError: myApp is not defined` and see a broken page. server.py detect_profile_domains uses model 'claude-sonnet-4-6' — confirm this identifier is still valid in the emergentintegrations LlmChat lib. If it fails, ai_domains stays empty (non-blocking as documented).

server.py _job_match_score awards +3 when tl in cat OR cat in tl. `cat in tl` (e.g. cat='' in tl='tech') triggers +3 for every tag because empty string is in every string. Guarded by `if tl and (tl in cat or (cat and cat in tl))` — cat check is present, good.

CandidateDashboard.js sets section='profile' on every reload when profile.profile_completed is false — good UX; but it silently overrides any explicit user click (e.g., candidate clicks 'Mes postulations', /profile response arrives late and switches back to 'profile'). Consider only auto-setting on first mount, not every loadAll().

rca of the issue: JobDetail.js was authored referencing `myApp` in the conditional-render tree without ever declaring it via useState nor fetching from /applications/me. In React, referencing an undeclared identifier during render throws ReferenceError, which unmounts the whole component. Any candidate visiting a job page would see either a blank page or the error boundary. Reproduction: login as candidate, click any job card, page crashes. Fix: add `const [myApp,setMyApp]=useState(null)` and a second useEffect that GETs /applications/me and setMyApp((data||[]).find(a=>a.job_id===id)||null), depending on [id,user,done] so it refreshes after a successful apply. Verified: JobDetail now renders for anonymous (login prompt), for candidate-without-application (form visible), for candidate-with-application (already-applied block with StatusBadge visible).
